name: allmaps/allmaps
content: # Allmaps 100,000s of maps are available through [IIIF](https://iiif.io/), across libraries, archives and museums worldwide. Allmaps makes it easier and more inspiring to **curate, georeference and explore collections of digitized maps**. 👉 For more information about the Allmaps project, see [allmaps.org](https://allmaps.org/). [![Allmaps Viewer](static/allmaps-viewer.jpg)](https://viewer.allmaps.org/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fannotations.allmaps.org%2Fmaps%2F9c4e14c0b9d41379) ## Contents Allmaps is an open source project and consists of multiple apps, packages and workers, all written in TypeScript and contained by this monorepo. Apps: - [Allmaps Editor](apps/editor) - [Allmaps Viewer](apps/viewer) - [Allmaps Latest](apps/latest) - [Allmaps CLI](apps/cli) - [Allmaps Explore](apps/explore) - [Allmaps Here](apps/here) Packages: - [@allmaps/annotation](packages/annotation) - [@allmaps/basemap](packages/basemap) - [@allmaps/id](packages/id) - [@allmaps/iiif-parser](packages/iiif-parser) - [@allmaps/leaflet](packages/leaflet) - [@allmaps/maplibre](packages/maplibre) - [@allmaps/openlayers](packages/openlayers) - [@allmaps/render](packages/render) - [@allmaps/schemas](packages/schemas) - [@allmaps/stdlib](packages/stdlib) - [@allmaps/tailwind](packages/tailwind) - [@allmaps/transform](packages/transform) - [@allmaps/triangulate](packages/triangulate) - [@allmaps/types](packages/types) - [@allmaps/ui](packages/ui) Workers: - [Allmaps Tile Server](workers/tileserver) - [Allmaps Preview Server](workers/preview) To see how these components are related, check out the [dependency graph](https://observablehq.com/@allmaps/javascript-dependencies). ## Contributing We're welcoming contributions! You can read more about the many ways you can contribute [here](./CONTRIBUTING.md). ## License - **Apps**: all apps are licensed under the [GPL-3.0](https://opensource.org/licenses/GPL-3.0) license, except the homepage and the CLI, which are licensed under the [MIT](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT) license. - **Packages**: all packages are licensed under the [MIT](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT) license. - **Workers**: all workers are licensed under the [MIT](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT) license. - **Data**: georeference data published through the Allmaps project is licensed under the [CC0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) license - **Base map**: [ODbL](https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/), © [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright) contributors. See Protomap's [licensing and attribution guidelines](https://github.com/protomaps/basemaps?tab=readme-ov-file#licensing-and-attribution-guidelines) for more details. ## Installation Make sure you have Node.js (version 24 or higher) and [pnpm 12](https://pnpm.io/installation) installed. This repository pins its pnpm version in `package.json`. Then, clone this repository locally: ```sh git clone https://github.com/allmaps/allmaps.git cd allmaps ``` For app development, initialize the apps and their dependencies: ```sh pnpm run init:apps ``` This installs workspace dependencies, builds only the workspaces the apps depend on, and runs app checks (including SvelteKit initialization). The current apps do not depend on `@allmaps/render-wasm`, so this workflow does not require Rust or wasm-pack. It does not build every app for production; dependencies that also contain an app or demo still run their existing build scripts. ### Package development and full setup Building all packages requires [Rust and Cargo](https://rust-lang.org/tools/install/) and [wasm-pack](https://wasm-bindgen.github.io/wasm-pack/installer/) in addition to Node.js and pnpm. These compile `@allmaps/render-wasm`, which is used by the preview and tileserver workers. Install Rust using rustup, then install wasm-pack using its installer or `cargo install wasm-pack`. To install dependencies, build all packages, and run package checks: ```sh pnpm run init:packages ``` For the existing full setup, including production app builds: ```sh pnpm run init ``` The `init` script is a shorthand for the following commands: 1. `pnpm install --recursive`: install all dependencies for all packages and apps. 2. `pnpm run build:packages`: build all packages, including TypeScript, Svelte, and Rust/WASM outputs. 3. `pnpm run check`: run workspace checks and initialize SvelteKit apps. 4. `pnpm run build:apps`: build apps and their dependencies. If things stop working later on, rerun the initialization script for your workflow. ### API development For local API development with PGlite or PostgreSQL, see the [local API workflow](tools/apis/README.md). `pnpm dev:apis` defaults to the local PGlite database; use `--db=postgres` to connect through `DATABASE_URL`, including to Neon. Supply a development database URL, never the main or production URL. The workflow also includes offline migration generation and manual local migrations with `pnpm db:migrate --db=pglite`. Run `pnpm setup:env` (or `pnpm setup:env --db=postgres`) to configure missing local settings while preserving existing values. GitHub login is optional. For automatic Neon migrations and coordinated API deployments on `develop` and `main`, see [API migrations and releases](.github/API_RELEASES.md), including the one-time setup and separate release enable switches. Development tools are grouped by responsibility: [API runner](tools/apis/README.md), [demo seed](tools/seed/README.md), [environment setup](tools/setup/README.md), and [IIIF fixture server](tools/iiif-server/README.md). Integration tests remain in [test/apis](test/apis/README.md), using temporary PGlite databases and local fixtures. ### App development After `pnpm run init:apps`, watch and rebuild app dependencies in one terminal: ```sh pnpm run watch:apps ``` Start the app you are working on in another terminal: ```sh pnpm --filter "@allmaps/viewer" run dev ``` You can also run `pnpm run dev` from the app's directory. To deliberately start all app development servers, use `pnpm run dev:apps`. To build apps and their dependencies for production, use `pnpm run build:apps`. To prepare only one app instead of all apps, select its dependency graph: ```sh pnpm install --recursive pnpm exec turbo run build --filter "@allmaps/viewer^..." pnpm exec turbo run check --filter "@allmaps/viewer" ``` Then use `pnpm exec turbo watch build --filter "@allmaps/viewer^..."` in the first terminal and the app's `dev` command in the second. The `^...` selector includes dependencies without selecting the app itself. ### Package development After `pnpm run init:packages`, watch and rebuild all packages in one terminal: ```sh pnpm run watch:packages ``` To run package demos and playgrounds, start their development servers in another: ```sh pnpm run dev:packages ``` Only packages with a `dev` script start a server. You can also start one playground with, for example, `pnpm --filter "@allmaps/render" run dev`. Use `pnpm run build:packages` for a one-time build of all packages. For a single package, build and watch just that package and its dependencies: ```sh pnpm install --recursive pnpm exec turbo run build --filter "@allmaps/transform..." pnpm exec turbo watch build --filter "@allmaps/transform..." ``` The trailing `...` includes the selected package and its dependencies. This example does not require Rust because `@allmaps/transform` does not depend on `@allmaps/render-wasm`. The existing root commands remain available: `pnpm run init` performs the full setup described above, `pnpm run build` builds all workspaces, and `pnpm run watch` watches packages and APIs. Prefer the scoped workflows for app or package work. ## Troubleshooting If things don't work, it might help to reinitialize the SvelteKit apps: ```sh pnpm run check ``` Or, reinstall dependencies and create the monorepo's symlinks: ```sh pnpm install -r ``` As a last resort, you can try to remove some (or all) `node_modules` directories using [npkill](https://npkill.js.org/): ```sh pnpm dlx npkill ``` ## Commit changes This repository uses [Husky](https://typicode.github.io/husky/) to run type checking, code linting and tests before each commit. To skip these tests, you can use git's `--no-verify` option: ```sh git commit --no-verify ``` ## Check formatting and types Check TypeScript types for all packages: ```sh pnpm run types ``` Run [Prettier](https://prettier.io/) and [ESLint](https://eslint.org/) for all packages: ```sh pnpm run lint ``` ## Run tests Run tests for all packages and apps: ```sh pnpm run test ``` Run tests for a single package: ```sh pnpm --filter "@allmaps/transform" test ``` You can run the tests from the package's directory instead: ```sh cd packages/transform pnpm test ``` # Versioning & publishing Create prerelease versions: ```sh pnpm run version-prerelease ``` Publish beta versions to npm: ```sh pnpm run publish-beta ```
